summary: Csaba Kiss is an indology and religious studies scholar. He earned his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (2003–2009) under Alexis Sanderson and has held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2021–2024) and Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).

Cuilan Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. She has held posts as Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies at Emmanuel College, Toronto (attested 2017) and at the University of Munich (attested 2018).
Cuma Ozkan is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. He earned a Master of Arts at the University of Iowa under the supervision of Morten Schlütter (attested 2013).
Cunda studied under Ajahn Pasanno and Ajahn Amaro.

Cuong T. Mai specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He completed an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi and a PhD under John R. McRae at Indiana University Bloomington, later serving as Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Vermont.

Cynthea J. Bogel is a scholar in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral studies under John M. Rosenfield and held an attested post at the University of Washington in 2009.

Cynthia Col is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Tibetology. She was a student in Chinese religion at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 2003) and studied under Mark Elliott and Steven D. Goodman.
Cynthia M. Beall is a Tibetology scholar who studied at Pennsylvania State University (~1971–1976). She joined the faculty at Case Western Reserve University in 1976.

Cynthia Talbot is an Indologist and historian. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1980–1988) and has served at the University of Texas at Austin (~1995), where she is Professor Emeritus.

Cyril Henry Philips was a historian and Indologist. He studied at the University of Liverpool (1931–1934) and SOAS (~1935–1940), later serving as SOAS Director (1957) succeeding Ralph Lilley Turner, and as Vice-Chancellor of the University of London (1972–1976).

Cyrus Stearns is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an MA under Turrell V. Wylie and a PhD under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp at the University of Washington (-1996), later working as a translator for the Tsadra Foundation.
Cécile Ducher specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD under Matthew T. Kapstein at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (-2017), where she is a research fellow.

D. C. Lau was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy who studied at the University of Hong Kong and the University of Glasgow. He held positions at SOAS, University College London, University of London, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (1978–1989).
D. C. Sarasvati was an Indologist who studied under V. Raghavan and served as Lecturer-cum-Research Assistant at the University of Madras (1964–1965).
D. L. Narasimhachar was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1927–1932) and held a post at the University of Mysore (~1932–1962).

D. Max Moerman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held posts at Barnard College (attested 2007–2008) and Columbia University (attested 2026), serving as Professor and Chair of Asian and Middle Eastern Cultures at Barnard.
D. N. Shukla was an Indology scholar who completed a D.Litt. at the University of Lucknow under K. A. Subramania Iyer. He held a post at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1958).

D. Neil Schmid is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, Waseda University, and the University of Pennsylvania, where he pursued doctoral studies under Victor H. Mair.

D. Phillip Stanley is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano. He has served as associate professor at Naropa University and Co-Director of Nitartha Institute (attested 2019).

Dagfinn Føllesdal was a philosopher and linguist. He studied at the University of Oslo and Harvard University under Willard Van Orman Quine. He taught at Harvard (1961–1964) and held posts at the University of Oslo and Stanford University (1968–2011).
